author: LaineyGossip
title: Mailbag for December 12, 2025
text:
(Marechal Aurore/ABACA/Anthony Harvey/Casey Flanigan/imageSPACE/ Chelsea Lauren/Shutterstock) Dear Squawkers,
It started back in the spring, when Ryan Coogler’s Sinners came out and shocked the fuck out of Hollywood with how it performed at the box office, grossing over $350 million at the worldwide box office with virtually no dip in earnings between its first and second weekend of release. And even in its third week it was still cooking. The film is now the “ highest-grossing original live-action movie in 15 years ” behind only Inception , by Christopher Nolan, who was thanked by Coogler in the credits to the film.
This week, Nolan, perhaps the most commercially successful auteur director in the business, hosted a screening for Sinners , which is huge at this time of year when everyone’s campaigning for Oscar nominations; during the event, Nolan told Coogler that the Irish River Dance scene was “the most spectacular musical inversion since Kubrick’s ‘Singin’ in the Rain,’ [from A Clockwork Orange ]”.
It’s great to see that these two filmmakers share this kind of friendship, and especially at a time when corporations are jeopardising art, Nolan and Coogler have both proved, time and again, that their stories can speak to the human condition and find a massive audience to appreciate them. It is extraordinary, and not hyperbolic, that an original film like Sinners performed the way it did at the multiplex. Not based on a video game or a toy or a comic book but pure, wonderful imagination and lived experience.
So…um…why are some people being so fucking weird about Sinners and its success? And it’s been months of this shit, starting when the movie premiered, with Variety ’s shadily worded tweet about the box office.
Variety’s shady tweet about Sinners This prompted a strong reaction – and not just from regular degulars but Hollywood creatives, like Ben Stiller, who straight up called Variety out.
For comparison, One Battle After Another opened with about $48 million worldwide, against a budget that is reportedly MORE THAN DOUBLE that of Sinners . And right now, it’s probably just breaking even. You think Variety tweeted about it the same way? Please.
Here’s how they tweeted about Christy , Sydney Sweeney’s movie that hard-flopped upon release.
Christy was such a bomb that it set a record for the most precipitous second week drop and is now in the top 10 for worst openings ever for a movie. And I’m not saying this to dump on Sydney, the point is Variety ’s bizarrely negative take on a movie that was actually a major fucking win at a time when there’s so much angst about the box office but not applying that attitude to movies that are less commercially successful…?
That was months ago, Lainey, why are we still talking about it? Well, we’re still talking about it because it comes as a part of a package.
Last week Rolling Stone released their list of the best movies of 2025 which included Eddington , which was a bust this summer, and Sinners as a no-show. This week Variety did their best of the year film list and, also, no Sinners .
To be clear, film criticism as we have said over and over again is important, and film critics have a right to share their unbiased opinions. Art is subjective, it is possible for a critic to not like a film that so many people did. And if I truly believe that is what I thought was happening here, I would support Rolling Stone and Variety ’s right to publish any list and exclude any film they want.
Ryan Coogler and Michael B. Jordan attend the ‘Sinners’ film premiere in London, UK on April 14, 2025 (Anthony Harvey/Shutterstock) But I’m not convinced that that’s what this is – not when we saw how Variety reported on Sinners all those months ago, and especially not when you consider that both Rolling Stone and Variety are owned by the same media company, Penske. Coincidence or conspiracy?
As Sarah has mentioned a few times at LaineyGossip, Ryan Coogler’s ownership deal with Warner Bros for his film was controversial from the jump. I mean, it shouldn’t be controversial that he’d want to own his own work in 25 years, but in the weeks following its release, there was reporting that industry executives were sniping about this agreement, calling it a “ very dangerous precedent ” – and this made headlines, it was a major conversation back in April because Sinners was such a smash hit.
Given its critical reception and commercial success, Sinners became an early Oscar contender and has remained a frontrunner, alongside One Battle After Another , which is undeniably the favourite in the race. And both films are Warner Bros titles. So, if you want to call it this, let’s put on our tin-foil hats.
Because, of course, what’s the biggest story in Hollywood right now? Warner Bros and the Netflix bid and the hostile counterbid by Paramount. The studio is so attractive to both Netflix and Paramount for its library – all those HBO shows, all those classic films, and…all the recent hits. Including a hit that, in 25 years, will revert back to the filmmaker who wrote and directed it. Should that film win the Best Picture Oscar, that would only increase its value, wouldn’t it?
Let’s dig into the mailbag…
Question from Kathryn DeVinney:
Question (plea, beg, desperate ask) for Lainey: I need all the details about Heated Rivalry. THIS is why streamers should release episodes week-to-week, to make sure we are salivating and READY for the next one. Were Connor and Hudson as hot and charming IRL? Spill, please!!!!
Lainey’s Answer:
Hot? Yes. Charming IRL? Yes.
For those who aren’t aware, I moderated the Q&A with Hudson Williams, Connor Storrie, and showrunner Jacob Tierney at the Heated Rivalry Toronto premiere a few weeks ago which means I met and spoke with all three backstage and onstage at the event. Here I am with the actors on the red carpet.
Elaine Lui on Instagram: “Horny Alert: HEATED RIVALRY premieres…
I’m starting on the carpet because I was so impressed with how they handled it. This wasn’t a frenzied premiere situation the way we see with huge Hollywood productions but there were still a lot of people there, fans of Rachel Reid’s books gathered on the ground floor of the TIFF Lightbox, and a very healthy turnout of Canadian media waiting to talk to them under the lights. For Hudson and Connor who were, at the time, relative unknowns, this would have been their most high-key PR moment. And they not only handled it, they sailed through it. With cheeky and playful soundbites, with quick quips, with just the right amount of enthusiasm but not too much thirst. Enough thirst though – this is a horny ass show, the thirst is a requirement.
Hudson Williams and Connor Storrie attend ‘The Actors Night’ hosted by The Actor Awards & Elle in West Hollywood, California on December 11, 2025 (Chelsea Lauren/Shutterstock) They were excited about their moment, a moment that, as actors, this is the goal, right? Knowing that your work will be seen on a new scale? And still, as new as they were, there was no sign of discomfort or any amateur vibes. These two were smooth, so smooth you would have thought they’d done it before. I really enjoyed the whole vibe but, even more than that, I respected it. I respected that their attitude, as a reflection of the show they’re promoting, about two queer hockey players, was fun and flirty and sexy. This has been one of the keys to the breakout success of Heated Rivalry , what Jacob deserves so much credit for in how he set the tone for the show. That’s not to say that they aren’t taking the work seriously, but that doesn’t mean it can’t be frothy. It doesn’t mean it can’t go down easy. And also, they go down on each other a lot, lol.
Here’s what did surprise me and this is superficial – I find Hudson and Connor so much more attractive in person ,which actually isn’t that superficial because it goes back to how well the show is made. Shane and Ilya aren’t actors, they’re athletes. They’re not supposed to look like they travel with a glam squad. Hudson and Connor, however, are actors. And when they are themselves, in real life, they look like actors: shiny and glowing. Like straight from a magazine editorial. Hudson especially. Which speaks to his talent because Shane, as a character, doesn’t have a lot of swag. Hudson, the person, is swaggy as fuck. The way he carries his body, how he walks, his eye contact…there’s less Shane in Hudson and more Ilya. And none of that comes through in the performance you see on screen.
Question from Maggie :
I’d love to hear your thoughts on Kristen Stewart’s comments about male actors/method acting. Is the hyper active style of Tom Cruise and over the top performance of ‘cool’ by Brad Pitt their own forms of method acting to make it more masculine? Similar with Jim Carrey and Will Ferrell and their over the top comedic performances? It got me thinking – so many male actors have a ‘thing’ that they do to set them apart, and Kristen’s observation that acting is fundamentally vulnerable and submissive, and therefore not masculine, puts this in a whole new light for me.
Sarah’s answer:
For reference, here is KStew talking about dudes and acting, and here is the specific quote, prompted by a discussion of Marlon Brando mispronouncing “Krypton” in Superman :
“Performance is inherently vulnerable and therefore quite embarrassing and unmasculine. There’s no bravado in suggesting that you’re a mouthpiece for someone else’s ideas. It’s inherently submissive. Have you ever heard of a female actor that was method?”
She goes into greater depth in the interview, which is worth a read, suffice to say: I agree with KStew. It’s not that there aren’t women who subscribe to Method acting (Lady Gaga leaps to mind) but definitely women can’t talk as openly about it as men. Natalie Portman once called Method acting “ a luxury women can’t afford ”, getting at the same point as KStew, that a woman behaving as Method actors do would be called a crazy bitch (at best).
Kristen Stewart attends the 2025 SFFILM Awards at Gateway Pavilion on December 8, 2025 in San Francisco on December 8, 2025 (Casey Flanigan/imageSPACE/ Shutterstock) I don’t think Tom Cruise or Brad Pitt really qualify as Method actors, though Pitt has used Method acting for certain roles, and he recounted a “ Method acting fail ” to the Kelce brothers on New Heights . Fine, whatever.
Definitely, Cruise and Pitt both base their celebrity personas on typically masculine ideals. Cruise is the cool jock, into motorcycles and planes and go fast, and Pitt is the laid-back artist who still gives off “I watch football” vibes. Or at least, that’s what they try to do. I think as they’ve aged, they’ve been less successful in maintaining these personas, and no matter how hard he tries, Tom Cruise cannot hide his dorkiness.
And while Jim Carrey has definitely done Method acting (see also: The Man in the Moon ), Will Ferrell is just like that. He’s a real comedian, he’s doing bits whether there’s an audience or not. Comedians will always be doing bits, it has nothing to do with acting. Just listen to Conan O’Brien and Will Arnett talk about the bit Conan was doing the week his parents died . It’s dark! But even then, Conan was doing a bit for an audience of one, just because…that’s who he is. Will Ferrell is like that, it has nothing to do with acting.
Circling back to KStew’s comment, though, I think part of explaining men and Method acting is that they’re embarrassed to do a non-physical job. That’s why they’re always trying to make acting about body transformation and extreme diets and bench pressing. They’re ashamed of doing a “soft” job, so they try to make it hard.
Question from Vitally Useless:
For LaineyGossip, how was your experience working as press at CCXP? I’ve heard that press at San Diego Comic Con are treated like cattle with little care as to whether or not they get decent face time with the actors and are often left waiting for long stretches of time unless they are there with a big outlet like Entertainment Weekly which throws its own events to ensure that they get face time with the actors.
Lainey’s Answer:
I haven’t been to San Diego Comic-Con in over a decade so I don’t really know what it’s like now but back when I was covering it for ETALK, yes, it wasn’t my favourite assignment as a reporter – a lot of waiting, a lot of disorganisation, I can’t say that I miss it. So, for sure, in comparison, I prefer CCXP. But then again, to be fair, it’s not exactly apples to apples.
Whenever I was at Comic-Con in the past, it was on a standard media pass, so the access level was different. For CCXP last week in São Paulo, we were invited by Amazon Prime like it was a junket, the junket just happened to be at CCXP. Prime had two major shows there to promote: Fallout (season two premieres next week) and The Boys . So it was already a guarantee that we would be able to interview the talent the way it works on the junket. But also, as part of it, Prime set it up that we could experience the expo and secured our passes for the convention so there were no restrictions on other content that we were covering. Which meant that we could attend panels and shoot footage about titles that were not just on Prime – like the new Game of Thrones spinoff, Marty Supreme , and more.
Overall, the time management was much more efficient. There were a couple of panels that we had to line up for but that’s pretty standard, our goal was to get into the panels, and we did, easily, with our passes. As a member of the media, then, whose job it is to report on the various projects being showcased at the expo, in our case since our attendance was facilitated by Prime, the logistics part of the work was close to ideal.
That doesn’t mean it wasn’t a hustle though. There is SO much to cover at CCXP. I’m sure you saw from social media and other outlets, there was a big celebrity presence at the convention, and the convention hall is huge. The panels are back-to-back to back. Between that, and the junkets, and shooting the activations and interviewing fans, we were non-stop, there for four straight days and pretty much no breaks. Plus…the commuting.
Here’s what I learned about CCXP in São Paulo that I did not know before we arrived that I would like to pass onto anyone who might be going: the traffic in São Paulo is bonkers. There was a shuttle taking us from the hotel to the convention centre every day, and the distance between the two was about 11km/6 miles. On average it took us 90 minutes to get there, one way, at various times of the day. As a citizen of Toronto though, lol, let me even that shit out because it’s not like it isn’t that way here. In downtown Toronto, it can sometimes take 45 minutes to go two blocks. So I’ll amend what I just said with this: if you are covering CCXP in São Paulo or TIFF in Toronto, build in time for traffic!
Question from Kaylyn :
sarah has talked a lot about how film press and appearances are all negotiated and contracted when actors sign onto their roles. since stranger things has come back, ive been thinking about how david harbour has been almost completely absent from season 5 promo, clearly a reaction to all the bad press he’s gotten regarding lily allen’s album about their divorce and then whatever happened between him and MBB on set (if anything). is the cancellation of press and appearances something that also has to be negotiated with agents and lawyers and such, or does the studio PR get the final say in that
Sarah’s answer:
I don’t think David Harbour’s absence from Stranger Things promo has all that much to do with Lily Allen torching his reputation. Harbour is really busy right now, making two movies while also launching Stranger Things ’ final season. Here he is at the season five premiere on November 6, and here he is just four days later, back on set . So while the younger cast of Stranger Things moved on to the UK for a premiere event in London on November 13, Harbour was working in New Jersey. (He’s starring in Evil Genius , Courteney Cox’s film about the pizza delivery bomb-collar case.)
David Harbour attends the ‘Stranger Things’ Season 5 World Premiere in Los Angeles on November 6, 2025 (Chelsea Lauren/Shutterstock) Besides that, Winona Ryder isn’t front and center, either. She was also not at the UK event in November. For sure, Netflix would have known about Harbour’s commitments—he probably made those commitments knowing well in advance he would not be expected to do the heavy lifting for season five promo, which is being carried mainly by the younger cast. But two things can be true—David Harbour was never expected to anchor this press tour, and no one is sad he’s staying out of the spotlight right now.
Now, someone I DO think got disinvited from press is Jeremy Renner, who has missed all the Wake Up Dead Man press in the last six weeks, since he was accused of threatening to call ICE on and sending unsolicited intimate photos to filmmaker Yi Zhou. Renner is not currently working, he should be available for Dead Man press, but it’s crickets. In this case, yes, I think Netflix rearranged his schedule, and they would have the final say, as the entity paying for everything.
Question from leah:
With the whole Winter/Jungkook “controversy” – I’m wondering if the Blackpink girls are immune to this drama? I haven’t seen any discourse (but maybe I just haven’t been paying attention) to Lisa and her french dude and Rose and her video guy. Is it because they’re dating western guys who aren’t in the kpop ecosystem?
Lainey’s Answer:
Trust me, there is mess out there over Lisa and Frédéric Arnault, people who don’t think he’s attractive enough for her and commentary that’s a lot grosser related to her motivations. If you’re not seeing it, I’m happy for you, because my algorithm serves me that shit all the time. So I don’t know that the BLACKPINK girls are “immune to this drama” but I would agree that it didn’t seem to be as disturbing when Jennie and V were dating a few years ago than whatever is or isn’t happening between Winter and Jung Kook. Not to say there wasn’t a bit of a meltdown but also, Jennie kinda has a IDGAF attitude with respect to her romances – and she’s actually had a few that we know of, which is more than we can say about most K-pop idols.
Lisa attends the Louis Vuitton Womenswear Spring-Summer 2025 show as part of Paris Fashion Week, in Paris, France on October 01, 2024 (Marechal Aurore/ABACA/Shutterstock) As I alluded to when I posted about the JK and Winter situation , though, there are some people who think that there’s a conspiracy going on in the background. Lots of theories about how this story is a distraction so that the media in Korea won’t focus on whatever they think the bigger and real scandal is. Several celebrities have currently been the target of media coverage that has crossed the line into shaming. Just in the last 24 hours, PSY (“Gangnam Style”) has been dragged onto the front page, somehow exposed for violating medical laws. There’s some discourse online right now that this can’t be an accident, that the social networks in Korea are being rigged so that the public focuses on the celebrity issues and not the more pressing ones. Some are also suggesting that there is bot activity happening that’s amplifying the speculation and backlash against JK and Winter. It’s getting harder and harder to pick through all of it, and Winter’s label, SM Entertainment, just issued a statement this week declaring legal action against the trolls online who’ve been spreading disinformation.
While we’re here, though, something very interesting and semi-related has just come up and it’s worlds colliding. This is related to New Jeans and Min Hee-jin, their producer. New Jeans was signed to ADOR, a subsidiary of HYBE, and there’s been two years of back and forth over the group’s rights and Min Hee-jin’s management, with accusations of a hostile takeover and backstabbing and undermining, and it basically killed all of the NJZ momentum.
Let me connect the worlds now…
Up until just a few months ago, Scooter Braun was the CEO of HYBE America. HYBE America owns a majority share in a company called TAG PR. If that sounds familiar, it’s because TAG PR is the crisis PR firm owned by Melissa Nathan that represents Justin Baldoni and he and TAG are both being sued by Blake Lively. Blake is claiming that Justin sexually harassed her and that he and TAG orchestrated a smear campaign against her. I’m sure we don’t have to rehash this fuckery but where it’s relevant is that in one of the many court filings related or adjacent to this case …
Min Hee-jin’s name just came up because, allegedly, she’s one of a group of people that TAG PR was allegedly running an online smear campaign against, allegedly. Her name has been included to establish a pattern of attack that TAG PR allegedly uses to protect and defend their clients.
There are many, many, MANY offshoot discussions we can have related to these…allegations and associations and more. We’ll save that for another time and for when more information and insight come to light with more filings and counter-filings.
